source_text: Καί τις ὀνόματι Ναόδωρος — ὁ καὶ Ἀπελλῆς — πατὴρ πόλεως, καὶ ἄλλος τις, νεωκόρος, ἐμμανόμενος καὶ αὐτὸς τῇ ἀσεβείᾳ τῶν εἰδώλων, ἠξίωσαν τὸν ἡγεμόνα δοθῆναι αὐτοῖς βοήθειαν, ὥστε ζητῆσαι ἐν οἷς ὑπώπτευον τόποις. Καί τις βοηθὸς ὀνόματι Ὠριγένης, ἐπιβὰς καὶ αὐτὸς σὺν τῷ προειρημένῳ Ναοδώρῳ μετὰ καὶ εἰρηναρχικῆς τάξεως καὶ ἑτέρων τινῶν, ηὗρον τὸν μακάριον Κόνωνα ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ λεγομένῳ Καρμενᾷ, βασιλικὸν ἐπαρδεύοντα κῆπον. Καὶ ἐγγίσαντες τῷ τρισμακαρίῳ μάρτυρι ἠσπάζοντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Χαῖρε, Κόνων. Καὶ ὁ τοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος, ἡ ἀκέραιος ψυχή, ὁ ἄκακος τῇ διανοίᾳ, λέγει πρὸς αὐτούς· Χαίρετε καὶ ὑμεῖς, τέκνα. Ὁ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ὠριγένης· Παπία, καλεῖ σε ὁ ἡγεμών. Ὁ ἅγιος Κόνων λέγει· Καὶ ἐμοῦ ὁ ἡγεμὼν τί χρείαν ἔχει, ξένου ἀνθρώπου καὶ μάλιστα Χριστιανοῦ; Ἐὰν ζητῇ τοὺς ὁμοίους ἑαυτοῦ, ζητείτω, καὶ οὐχὶ ἄνθρωπον γεωπόνον, μοχθοῦντα τὸ καθ᾽ ἡμέραν. Καὶ ἐπαπορηθεὶς ὁ παράνομος Ναόδωρος ἐπὶ τῇ ἀντιλογίᾳ τοῦ ἁγίου Κόνωνος, κελεύει δεθῆναι αὐτὸν τῷ ἵππῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ οὕτως ἕλκεσθαι. Καὶ ὁ ἅγιος μάρτυς οὐδὲν ἀντεῖπεν τοῖς ἐφέλκουσιν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ πράως καὶ ἐπιεικῶς ἐπηκολούθει τοῖς παρανόμοις.
thought_title: Searchers find Conon watering the garden and drag him away
orientation: After the city of Magydus is left deserted, Naodorus and Origen lead a party that finds the gardener Conon at Carmena.
pass_a_gloss: And a certain man by name Naodorus, the one also called Apelles, father of a city, and another certain man, a temple warden, himself also raving mad with the impiety of the idols, asked the governor that help be given to them, so that they might search in the places which they suspected. And a certain assistant by name Origen, having mounted also himself together with the aforesaid Naodorus with also a band of the irenarch and certain others, found the blessed Conon in a certain place called Carmena, watering an imperial garden. And having drawn near to the thrice blessed martyr they greeted him saying: Greetings, Conon. And the slave of Christ, the unblemished soul, the guileless in mind, says to them: Greetings also to you, children. Origen says to him: Old man, the governor calls you. The holy Conon says: And what need does the governor have of me, of a stranger man and especially of a Christian? If he seeks those like himself, let him seek, and not a man who is a gardener, toiling for the daily living. And having been at a loss, the lawless Naodorus, at the contradiction of the holy Conon, commands him to be bound to his horse and thus to be dragged. And the holy martyr answered nothing back to those dragging him, but gently and mildly he followed the lawless men.

vocative address to aged Conon here, not the proper name Papias the martyr from the previous section
fixed glossary English for humble day laborer in soil and garden
literal moral legal term used for Naodorus and the draggers, kept uniform

pass_b_english: Then a man named Naodorus — also called Apelles —, a father of a city, and another man, a temple warden who was himself raving mad with the impiety of the idols, asked the governor to give them help so they could search in the places they suspected. An assistant named Origen mounted up too with the Naodorus just mentioned, along with a peace-keeping detachment and some others, and they found blessed Conon at a place called Carmena, watering the imperial garden.

When they came up to the thrice-blessed martyr, they greeted him, saying, "Greetings, Conon." Conon, Christ's servant, a pure soul and harmless in mind, said to them, "Greetings to you too, children." Origen says to him, "Old man, the governor is calling for you." Holy Conon says, "What need does the governor have of me, a stranger and above all a Christian? If he wants people like himself, let him look for them, and not for a gardener who toils day by day."

Thrown by holy Conon's answer, lawless Naodorus ordered him to be tied to his own horse and dragged along like that. The holy martyr said nothing back to the men dragging him, but gently and meekly followed the lawless men.
